notes: Never got a 200. Three attempts, varying (a) whether pagination query params (p/per_page) were sent and (b) the issue_type path value ('jira-app' vs 'custom', both from the contract's declared enum: jira-app, azure, asana, linear, clickup, confluence, figma, devrev, gitlab, github, custom, trello) — all three returned the identical transport-level 500 {"status":500,"error":"Internal Server Error"} with no error body/code from the app itself (unlike the capability's own declared 400/401/403/404/500 shapes, which all carry {success:false, error:{code, message}} — this 500 doesn't even match the capability's own declared error schema). test_case_id was not guessed: it was resolved from the __readonly__ pool fixture (TC-54455 -> 1971631) via list_folder_test_cases_v1, and that same case's 'issues' field came back as an empty array on that read, i.e. this account/case has no tracker tickets linked at all. That is consistent with two different explanations this run cannot distinguish between: (1) the preprod account '<redacted>' has no external-tracker integration configured for any issue_type, and the handler crashes instead of returning a graceful empty/'not configured' response when it tries to resolve one; or (2) the endpoint is broken outright regardless of tracker configuration. Either way this is a genuine BLOCKED result, not a payload mistake on this end: the path params match the declared contract exactly (issue_type from the closed enum, test_case_id as the required integer, verified to belong to the fixture project/group), and varying both dimensions the contract exposes did not change the outcome. Did not try the other 10 issue_type values (azure, asana, linear, clickup, confluence, figma, devrev, gitlab, github, trello) beyond the 3-attempt cap the task sets; given 'jira-app' and 'custom' both failed identically, there is no reason from the evidence gathered to expect a different tracker type to succeed. Because no call ever succeeded, contract.declared_missing/undeclared_returned could not be computed against a real response and are left empty rather than guessed.
